svg.title: One form instance through the field tree
svg.desc: English reconstruction of the original explanatory diagram.

text.tspan: ENGLISH EDITION
One form instance through the field tree
1. The container creates the instance
The typed form hook creates one instance. The app's container
passes it to the form; it does not create a separate instance for every
shared field.
2. Form provides the context
The antd Form receives that instance. FormItem and shared input
components consume the existing form context rather than receiving
another form prop.
3. Choose how a field reads or writes
Use name for an ordinary bound Form.Item, a shouldUpdate render
prop for derived display, and useWatch when a field needs a
watched value. Use typed setters for coordinated writes.
4. Actions outside the form
Request buttons outside the Form tree can receive the instance
explicitly. They convert the current values for draft, inspection,
approval, rejection, or deletion requests.
Keep the boundaries distinct
Inputs share the editing instance. Typed field access checks the
editor's paths and values; response and request adapters check the
server boundaries separately.
English diagram redrawn from the original illustration.
Example values are illustrative; the original image remains archived.
